extracted.intended_audience: school and college administrators, Title IX coordinators, policymakers, and legal counsel for recipients of Federal financial assistance
extracted.subtask_description: Final Department of Education regulations and preamble describing legally binding obligations of recipients (K-12 and postsecondary) to respond to sexual harassment under Title IX, including definitions, triggering conditions, grievance-process requirements, supportive measures, and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt response by offering supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Promptly respond to individuals who are alleged to be victims of sexual harassment by offering supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must offer supportive measures when they have actual knowledge or receive a report; supportive measures are designed to restore or preserve a complainant's equal educational access. This obligation exists irrespective of whether a formal complaint is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair grievance process when investigation is initiated
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a fair grievance process to resolve sexual harassment allegations when a complainant requests an investigation or a Title IX Coordinator decides an investigation is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grievance process must give clear procedural rights to both parties and include procedural due process protections to ensure a fair and reliable factual determination. Recipients may initiate a grievance process either at complainant request or at the Coordinator's direction under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide remedies when respondent found responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient determines a respondent to be responsible for sexual harassment after following a fair grievance process, the recipient must provide remedies to the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies follow a fair determination of responsibility reached through the required grievance process; recipients must not treat respondents as responsible before affording due process protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define sexual harassment for Title IX purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the conduct constituting sexual harassment for Title IX purposes (see §106.30 Definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations adopt and adapt the Gebser/Davis framework and expressly include quid pro quo harassment and Clery Act/VAWA sex offenses in the definition so those offenses trigger a recipient's response without needing assessment of severity, pervasiveness, offensiveness, or denial of equal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify conditions that activate recipient's obligation to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the conditions that activate a recipient's obligation to respond to allegations of sexual harassment and impose a general standard for the sufficiency of a recipient's response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations set out the triggering conditions (e.g., actionable sexual harassment and actual knowledge) and require particular elements of a recipient's response, such as offering supportive measures, to satisfy the deliberate indifference standard adapted for administrative enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify conditions requiring initiation of a grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify conditions that require a recipient to initiate a grievance process to investigate and adjudicate allegations of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains when a formal complaint or other circumstances create an obligation to initiate the recipient's grievance process; the rule distinguishes between when supportive measures suffice and when formal grievance/adjudication is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish procedural due process protections in grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish procedural due process protections that must be incorporated into a recipient's grievance process to ensure a fair and reliable factual determination when investigating and adjudicating a formal complaint of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural protections include clear rights for both parties during investigation, adjudication, and appeals; the preamble emphasizes that recipients may not treat respondents as responsible without these protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures offered irrespective of formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to offer supportive measures to every complainant, irrespective of whether the complainant files a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation recognizes that a formal complaint is not required for a recipient to have actual knowledge or to be required to respond; supportive measures should be available immediately to restore or preserve equal educational access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint initiates grievance process but is not required for actual knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'formal complaint' is a document that initiates a recipient's grievance process, but a formal complaint is not required in order for a recipient to have actual knowledge of sexual harassment that activates the recipient's legal obligation to respond promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must distinguish between a formal complaint (which triggers the grievance-adjudication pathway) and earlier triggers of response obligations (which can require supportive measures and other responses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat respondent as responsible without due process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not treat a respondent as responsible for sexual harassment without providing due process protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations require that findings of responsibility be reached only after a fair grievance process; until such a determination, responses should avoid assigning culpability while offering protective/supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and dissemination requirements (Title IX Coordinator and policies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Update requirements for recipients to designate a Title IX Coordinator, disseminate the recipient's non-discrimination policy and the Title IX Coordinator's contact information, and notify students, employees, and others of the recipient's grievance procedures and grievance process for handling reports and complaints of sex discrimination, including sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure the Coordinator is identified and contact information and grievance procedures are publicly available; these administrative requirements facilitate actual knowledge and appropriate responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and adapt Gebser/Davis framework for administrative enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with the Gebser/Davis framework—definition of actionable sexual harassment, actual knowledge, and deliberate indifference—but adapt those elements for administrative enforcement under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department adopts the Supreme Court framework to ensure consistency between judicial and administrative enforcement while expanding definitions and standards (e.g., including quid pro quo and Clery/VAWA offenses, adapting actual knowledge and deliberate indifference) to suit administrative remedies and policy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include quid pro quo and Clery Act/VAWA sex offenses in sexual harassment definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt the Davis definition by also expressly including quid pro quo harassment and Clery Act/VAWA sex offenses so that these offenses trigger a recipient's response obligations without needing to be evaluated for severity, pervasiveness, offensiveness, or denial of equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inclusion ensures that inherently serious misconduct triggers required recipient responses immediately because prohibiting such conduct presents no First Amendment concerns and causes denial of equal educational access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge standard includes notice to Title IX Coordinator and K-12 employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Gebser/Davis concept of actual knowledge, adapted by including notice to any recipient's Title IX Coordinator, or notice to any elementary and secondary school employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adaptation furthers policy goals of ensuring elementary and secondary schools respond whenever a school employee knows of sexual harassment or allegations while respecting postsecondary students' autonomy about reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate indifference standard adapted with required actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the deliberate indifference standard adapted by specifying actions that every recipient must take in response to every instance of actual knowledge of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifying required actions (such as offering supportive measures) ensures recipients respond to restore or preserve equal educational access without second-guessing discretionary choices about sanctions or remedies in fact-specific circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions in §106.30 apply to entire 34 CFR part 106
rubrics_metrics.description: The definitions in §106.30 apply to the entirety of 34 CFR part 106; some provisions also explicitly refer to terms 'as defined in §106.30' to provide additional clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should treat §106.30 definitions as governing across all provisions of the part; references in the preamble and regulations use final regulation numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' Title IX processes must respect constitutional rights
rubrics_metrics.description: In responding to any claim of sex discrimination under Title IX, recipients are not required to deprive an individual of rights guaranteed under the U.S. Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble clarifies that Title IX enforcement and recipients' responses must be consistent with constitutional due process and other constitutional protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR authority to require remedial action
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirm that the Department's Office for Civil Rights (OCR) may require recipients to take remedial action for discriminating on the basis of sex or otherwise violating the Department's regulations implementing Title IX, consistent with 20 U.S.C. 1682.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR enforcement may include remedial steps up to termination of federal financial assistance in accordance with statutory authority and administrative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressly prohibit retaliation against individuals for exercising rights under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations include an explicit anti-retaliation provision (Section 106.71) to protect complainants, respondents, witnesses, and others who exercise Title IX rights or participate in grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirement for Title IX personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that Title IX Coordinators, investigators, and decision-makers must be properly trained (see Section 106.45(b)(1)(iii) reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble and regulatory text emphasize training for personnel involved in the grievance process to ensure fair, reliable investigations and determinations; training content and scope are addressed in the rule and accompanying sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge intersections with other laws and parental rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge the intersection of Title IX with Title VII and FERPA, as well as the legal rights of parents or guardians to act on behalf of individuals with respect to Title IX rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must consider overlapping legal obligations and the rights of parents/guardians when implementing policies and responding to reports under Title IX; the preamble recognizes these interactions but focuses on Title IX's obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious-institution exemption procedural change
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate the requirement that religious institutions submit a written statement to the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights to qualify for the Title IX religious exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This regulatory change updates the administrative procedure for claiming the religious exemption; recipients qualifying for the exemption should consult the regulation for current requirements.
